title: English File Upper-Intermediate, File 4: future perfect and continuous; conditionals and time clauses

fixIt.text: By 2030, I will have finish my degree.
fixIt.explain: Future perfect: will have + past participle.

fixIt.text: This time tomorrow I'll be lie on the beach.
Don't call at eight; we'll be have dinner.
fixIt.explain: In progress at a future time: will be + -ing.

fixIt.text: If you heat ice, it melted.
fixIt.explain: Zero conditional (always true): if + present, present.

fixIt.text: I'll tell you as soon as I heard the results.
fixIt.explain: After as soon as, use the present for the future.

fixIt.text: If you'll need anything, just call me.
fixIt.explain: No will after if: If you need anything …

fixIt.text: By the end of this year, we will have been live here for ten years.
fixIt.explain: will have been + -ing: how long, up to a future time.

fixIt.text: Provided that you finishes your homework, you can go out.

builder.text: The train will have left by then.
builder.tip: Future perfect: done before a future time.

builder.text: Call me as soon as you arrive.

radio.title: In ten years
radio.text: In ten years, I will have finished my studies, and I will probably be working in tourism. If everything goes well, I will have saved enough money to open a small guesthouse in Kampot. My husband says that by then he will have been teaching for fifteen years. As soon as our children are old enough, we will take them travelling. Unless something changes, we will be living by the river.
